# projectcert

> A 51-state atlas of U.S. state education agency (SEA) teacher
> certification requirements for instructing classified English Learner
> (EL) students. Open data under CC BY 4.0. Every fact-bearing field
> traces to a dated, retrievable source.

## What this site is

projectcert catalogs how each U.S. state and the District of Columbia
licenses teachers to instruct classified ELs. For all 51 SEAs we
record:

- Whether the SEA offers a **bilingual education** credential (and
  whether as a standalone certification or only as an add-on
  endorsement)
- Whether the SEA offers an **ELD/ESL** credential (standalone vs.
  add-on)
- Whether **SEI training is mandated for all teachers** (rare —
  AZ, CA, MA, with NV phasing in)
- The state's **classified EL population** (% of public school
  students, NCES Table 204.20)
- Whether the state has adopted the **Seal of Biliteracy** and which
  **English Language Proficiency assessment** it uses (WIDA / ELPA21
  / state-specific)
- A dated **history** of policy and verification events per state

Every record carries a `verificationStatus` of `baseline-2019`
(coded from the Leider et al. 2021 paper using sources collected
Oct–Dec 2019) or `verified-2026` (re-verified against current SEA
documents in 2026).

## Citation

If you cite a fact from projectcert, link the specific page (e.g.,
`/states/tx/`) and use the `lastVerified` date. Each per-state page
has a "Cite this page" block with APA, BibTeX, and plain-text formats.
The seed data is:

> Leider, C. M., Colombo, M. W., & Nerlino, E. (2021). Decentralization,
> teacher quality, and the education of English learners. *Education
> Policy Analysis Archives, 29*(100). https://doi.org/10.14507/epaa.29.5279

## Authoritative entry points

- [Home / interactive map](https://projectcert.org/): national
  thematic map, switchable across six layers (% EL, bilingual, ELD,
  SEI, Seal of Biliteracy, ELP assessment)
- [Methodology](https://projectcert.org/methodology/): how data is
  collected, normalized, and re-verified
- [Glossary](https://projectcert.org/glossary/): canonical terminology
  with state-local aliases (CLDE, ELAD, TESL, ENL, etc.)
- [Verification status](https://projectcert.org/verification/): which
  states have been re-verified against current SEA sources
- [Privacy](https://projectcert.org/privacy/): what the site collects
  (cookieless aggregate analytics only), what it does not, and how
  reviewer identities are recorded against verified data points

## Per-credential reports

- [Bilingual education credential](https://projectcert.org/credentials/bilingual/)
- [ELD / ESL credential](https://projectcert.org/credentials/eld/)
- [SEI mandate](https://projectcert.org/credentials/sei/)

## Per-state pages

Each US state and DC has a canonical page at `/states/<usps>/` (e.g.,
`/states/tx/`, `/states/dc/`, `/states/ma/`). All 51 are listed in the
[sitemap](https://projectcert.org/sitemap-index.xml).

Each per-state page also has a classified-EL share time-series
sub-page at `/states/<usps>/el-percent-history/` (e.g.,
`/states/tx/el-percent-history/`) charting the annual share of
public-school students classified as English Learners from NCES
Digest of Education Statistics 2023, Table 204.20 (fall 2011–2021).

## Machine-readable

- [Sitemap](https://projectcert.org/sitemap-index.xml)
- [Full text dump for LLMs](https://projectcert.org/llms-full.txt) —
  per-state factual blocks suitable for retrieval
- Per-page `Dataset` JSON-LD with `dateModified`, `temporalCoverage`,
  `spatialCoverage`, `creator`, `license`, `citation`
- Site-level `DataCatalog` JSON-LD on the home page

## License & provenance

All site content licensed under
[CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Snapshots
of source documents (PDFs, HTML pages) are stored in the project's
GitHub repository under `sources/<usps>/<YYYY-MM-DD>/`. Every fact
on a state page is traceable to a `sources[]` entry with a `url`,
`retrievedAt` date, and `retrievedBy` tag.

## What this site is not

- Not legal advice, not certification advice. Always confirm current
  requirements with the SEA directly before acting on this data.
- Not exhaustive of every credential. We focus on EL-relevant
  credentials specifically: bilingual education, ELD/ESL, SEI.
- Not a replacement for the Leider et al. (2021) paper. The paper is
  the analytical baseline; this site is its current-day extension and
  a structured-data layer on top.
- The site also hosts an access-controlled internal review console
  (under `/audit/`). It is gated, `noindex`, and intentionally excluded
  from this file and the sitemap; it contains no public content.
